findings.comment: Two proposed mitigation trees in the southeast corner are positioned 0 to 0.2 feet from the overhead electric distribution line along the south boundary. Measured distances fall far short of the required 15-foot minimum clearance for non-utility-compatible trees from distribution conductors.

Two proposed mitigation trees positioned 0 to 0.2 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor on the south boundary are within the prohibited 25-foot clearance zone for large trees (mature height 40+ feet). If these are Live Oak or Cedar Elm shade trees as indicated by the plant schedule, they fail the clearance requirement by a substantial margin.

applicableAreas: South boundary landscape area near utility poles
findings.comment: Two proposed mitigation trees positioned 0 to 0.2 feet from the overhead electric line on the south boundary are well within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone from electric utility poles marked along that overhead line.

The landscape plan and plant schedule do not explicitly identify or differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) by mature height. The plant list shows only minimum container heights (16' for shade trees, 8-10' for ornamental trees) at time of planting, not mature heights. The identity and mature height of species cannot be verified from available plan documentation.

While the landscape plan depicts the overhead electric line and proposed trees in proximity, there are no clearance dimensions, notes, or callouts on the plan documenting the spatial relationship or verifying compliance with minimum clearance distances. The trees are shown directly at or on the utility line without any documentation of measured distances or compliance verification.

Two proposed mitigation trees in the south boundary area are planted within prohibited clearance zones (0 to 0.2 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Plans show no approval letter or authorization for this variance from standard clearance requirements.
